subject: One-time pilot credit + structured discount request — Carely Health
messages:
From: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@carelyhealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot proposal and pricing ask

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team at Carely is excited about Redwood’s latency and cost profile for clinical workflows. We want to propose a 6-month pilot across three QA environments (ingest, triage, summary) and are trying to firm up commercial terms.

Quick ask: to get Exec buy-in and legal through the pilot timeline, we need a one-time credit and a structured discount if we commit to a 24-month usage minimum after the pilot. Proposed commercial outline from our side:
- One-time onboarding credit: $40k applied to first invoice
- Structured discount: 18% year-1 on listed consumption rates, drops to 12% year-2 contingent on minimum committed spend of $750k ARR equivalent across the two years
- Pilot anticipated token volume: 8M tokens/month during pilot; 30M tokens/month average post-pilot if full rollout

Can Redwood do a combined pilot credit + multi-year structured discount? If so, what guardrails would you require (audit rights, minimum usage, early termination recoup)? We’d like to move quickly — target start date first week of May.

Thanks,
Evan
Evan Brooks
Dir, Product Operations — Carely Health
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2027-04-03T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Pilot proposal and pricing ask — Carely (business case + modeling)

Team,

Looping you on Carely’s ask (below). TL;DR: they want a $40k onboarding credit + an 18% / 12% stepped discount tied to a 24-month commit with a $750k spend floor. Total deal opportunity (if full rollout) ~ $1.8M ARR over two years, but pilot is low-commit and the immediate revenue is small.

Why I’m escalating: they’re a strategic payer in the cardiology vertical and a public procurement process — winning this pilot quickly unlocks three other pilot opportunities via their systems integrator partner. I think a capped credit + conditional discount is defensible, but we need finance + contracts to sign the recoup and audit language.

Requested approvals / asks:
1) Marissa — VP/CFO sign-off on a one-time credit up to $40k with an agreed recoup schedule tied to the committed spend (I recommend recoup over 12 months if they miss the floor).
2) Karthik — commercial guardrails: minimum billed monthly usage to start recoup; SLA credit language; clause for automatic reversion to standard price if usage < 50% of projection after 3 months.
3) Monica (CS/legal touch) — confirm the SOW/contract timeline. Need a short SOW + audit clause and an optional early-termination recoup formula.

Attached: projected usage workbook (Carely_Projected_Usage_Q1-Q4.xlsx), draft SOW. I added a simple model showing net present value at different adoption curves.

If you want to discuss on a quick call, I’m free 2–4pm PT today. Otherwise, if Marissa is comfortable with the high-level approach I’ll send an official memo to Evan with the conditional structure.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Account Executive — Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-04T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot proposal and pricing ask — Carely (business case + modeling)

Rishi — thanks for the summary and for flagging strategic upside. I’m comfortable considering a targeted pilot credit + stepped discount but want tighter guardrails before I sign off.

Requested clarifications / mandatory conditions:
- Credit cap: approve up to $30k as a firm onboarding credit; authorizing the incremental $10k requires signed SOW + SI partner LOE commitments documented.
- Discount structure: approve a conditional 16% / 10% stepped discount (vs requested 18%/12%); discount only applies to billable consumption after the pilot period and is subject to an annual true-up.
- Commitment / recoup: client must commit to a minimum 24-month term and a $700k spend floor over those 24 months; if they fail to hit 80% of the floor after 12 months, we reserve the right to invoice the difference pro rata (recoup schedule over remaining months).
- Audit & usage verification: procurement must provide monthly usage reports and give Redwood 30-day window to request an independent audit if numbers diverge materially (>10%).
- Legal: include a 90-day pilot exit clause with a defined transfer-of-data process and IP protections.

Karthik — please run the NPV sensitivity for our model using 14–20% annual discount scenarios and attach the worst-case risk to ARR book. Monica — can you work with legal to draft the SOW addendum (1–2 pages) and the recoup language?

If the internal model with the $30k credit + 16%/10% conditional discount shows acceptable downside (<8% immediate ARR dilution in worst case), I’ll sign off and have corporate legal send a term memo to Carely (cc: procurement).

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
VP, Finance Operations — Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@carelyhealth.com>, Carely Health Procurement <procurement@carelyhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-05T16:38:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood conditional approval — Carely pilot credit & stepped discount (terms)

Evan / Carely team — thanks for the patience. After internal review we can approve the pilot structure with the following conditional commercial terms: 

1) Onboarding credit: $30,000 applied to the first invoice, payable after kickoff and delivery of the signed SOW; an incremental $10,000 discretionary credit may be approved once the SI partner LOE and kickoff deck are submitted and accepted by Redwood.
2) Stepped discount: 16% year-1, 10% year-2 on consumption post-pilot; discount only applies once the pilot is closed and invoicing has moved to production rates. Annual true-up to reconcile consumption vs committed minimums.
3) Minimum commitment: 24 months; $700,000 floor over the term. If Carely fails to deliver >=80% of the floor in the first 12 months, Redwood may recoup the difference pro rata over the remaining term.
4) Audit & verification: Carely will provide monthly usage exports; Redwood reserves the right to request a third-party usage verification if discrepancies >10%.
5) Pilot exit: 90-day exit clause for pilot with data export obligations and defined support window.

Next steps: Rishi — please share the short SOW and the SI partner LOE. Monica & Legal — please prepare a 1–2 page memo reflecting the above and a draft SOW addendum for signature. Evan — if Carely accepts, we’ll issue a term memo and attach the SOW for signature; we will apply the $30k onboarding credit on the first production invoice after SOW sign.

Best,
Marissa Cole
VP, Finance Operations — Redwood Inference

Attachments: Draft_SOW_Carely_Health_v1.docx (1 page draft); Carely_Projected_Usage_Q1-Q4.xlsx (model)
